rationale:
Evidence: iteration 5 (wheel_radius 0.03, mass 0.45, kp 4.2, kd 1.2, base 1.15) is the best raced design at 746. Oval and s-bend finish with margin (2.19 s, 2.50 s). The slalom times out in 20 of 20 trials at 0.87 progress, with almost no line loss (0 events) and max_error 0.033 m. So the robot tracks the line but is too slow for the 3 s limit. Iteration 6 showed base_speed is not the limit: raising it from 1.15 to 1.28 left slalom progress unchanged (0.872 to 0.868). Iteration 7 raised wheel_radius to 0.04 for about 33% more ground speed per PWM count, with kp 3.4 and kd 1.0. Oval and s-bend improved (945 and 940 mean), but the slalom failed early by going off track in 20 of 20 trials (progress 0.42, max_error 0.063). Turn gain per unit signal scales roughly as kp*wheel_radius/wheel_track. Iteration 5 gives 4.2*0.03/0.09 = 1.40. Iteration 7 gives 3.4*0.04/0.09 = 1.51, which is higher, and the extra speed and gain together pushed the robot off the line.

Changes: (1) wheel_radius 0.03 to 0.035 m, a smaller step (about 17% more ground speed) than iteration 7. (2) kp 4.2 to 3.6, so the effective turn gain is 3.6*0.035/0.09 = 1.40, the same as the stable iteration 5. (3) kd 1.2 to 1.1, scaled with kp to keep damping in proportion. (4) mass 0.45 to 0.40 (the contract minimum) for faster acceleration and quicker yaw response, since lower mass removed the off-track endings in iteration 5. (5) base_speed 1.15 to 1.25 to add some command headroom. Sensors, sensor size, ki and line_loss are unchanged.

Expected result: slalom progress rises from 0.87 toward 0.95 or more, with the first slalom completions possible. Oval and s-bend still finish with lower completion_time. Risks: the faster robot may leave the line on tight bends (off-track endings above about 4 of 20 would indicate this), and a smaller gain margin may increase the max_error on the slalom.

Hypotheses: H1, if the slalom still times out near 0.87 progress, the speed limit comes from turning losses, so the next test is kp about 3.2 with base 1.35. H2, if off-track endings rise above about 4 of 20, the speed is too high for the gain, so set base to 1.15 and kd to 1.3. H3, if steering_oscillation on the slalom exceeds about 0.5, kd is too low for this speed, so raise kd toward 1.3.

Measurements wanted: slalom progress and completion_time for speed margin, slalom max_error and line_loss_events for steering margin, and steering_oscillation with control_effort for damping.
